note: Every form of a given name, by language, with whether an archive has met it on a record. Built from data/given-name-families.json; nothing about a person is kept. A form with seen 0 is a lookup aid, not a finding.

notSame.why: Jesus / Jesús is the Greek-Latin form of Yeshua, a short form of Yehoshua (Joshua), not of Joseph; Spanish José is Joseph, Jesús is not.
A separate Hebrew name, Yehoshua ('YHWH is salvation'), not a form of Joseph (Hebrew Yosef, '(God) shall add'). Josué and Giosuè belong to Joshua.
Latin name with the same meaning; Gottlieb translates it but they are separate names.

Gottlieb is a German name coined as a translation of Greek Theophilos (and Amadeus) in Pietist circles; a calque, not the same name. Latin and Polish registers may nevertheless write Theophilus/Teofil for a Gottlieb.
A cognate German name from the same Proto-Germanic roots (Gunþ- + harjaz), but a separate name in registers.
Old Norse Gunnarr is the cognate name of the same legendary figure (gund + heri vs guðr + herr), a separate name today.
A Scottish Gaelic name, unrelated to Hector though usually anglicised as Hector.
Spanish given name from Latin germanus; a different name from Slavic German/Herman.

Irish name that is etymologically unrelated to Hugh; Hugh was used as its English replacement in anglicised records, so an Irish search for Hugh should also try Aodh, but it is not a spelling of Hugh.
Listed on the Hugh page only as a related name; a separate name (Germanic hug- plus beraht), not a spelling of Hugh.
Irish feminine name; Ida is used as its English anglicisation, but it is a separate name, not a spelling of Ida.
Old Norse goddess's name; the Ida page only says Ida 'may be related', so not treated as a form.
A different Russian name (from George); Wikipedia says 'Not to be confused with Yegor'.
Irish name that Wiktionary lists as the Irish equivalent of Jeremiah, but it is a different Gaelic name (Diarmuid); Jeremiah was used to anglicise it. A lead only, not a spelling.
A separate name (a queen who sacked Axum), not a variant of Judith.
Irish name Wiktionary lists beside Judith as an Irish counterpart, along with Siobhán; both are separate Irish names (Sheila/Joan) and not spellings of Judith.
Ethiopian name sometimes wrongly anglicised as Judith; not a form of it.
Wikipedia notes Lochlainn has been rendered into English as Lawrence, a historical substitution, not the same name.
Hebrew Elʿazar; Wiktionary lists it as the Hebrew translation for the given name, but it is the longer Hebrew name from which Lazarus is said to derive, a distinct register name.
In Dutch, Lia is a diminutive of Cornelia, a different name.
Leo may be a short form of Leonard (Germanic), a separate name.
Leo can be a short form of Leopold, but Leopold is a separate name (Germanic, Old High German Luitbald).
Different Germanic name (leon + hard), though both give the short form Leo.
A different word that the given name was later misassociated with.
Ladislav and László are names 'sometimes erroneously associated with Louis' but are a separate Slavic/Hungarian name.
Wikipedia says Mabel in Ireland was seen as a variant of the Celtic name Maeve, but they are separate names.
Calum/Callum (Scottish Gaelic, from Columba 'dove') is the saint's name itself; Wiktionary links the two but Malcolm is the 'devotee of Columba' compound, so they are separate names.
The masculine counterpart; a separate family in the catalogue.

A compound of Maria and Anna/Anne, a separate name (also Marie-Louise, Maria Elena).
The unrelated Roman masculine name Marius, not a form of Maria.
Wiktionary says Marina is possibly a variant of Maria in some etymologies, but Maria is a separate name.
The male Latin name (Marinus) from which Marina is the feminine; Wikipedia lists it as related, not as the same name.
Maurus ('Moor') is the Latin word Mauritius derives from and a name in its own right (St Maurus), not a form of Maurice.
Emilian/Aemilianus is the other Roman name from which Frederick III explained Maximilian; a separate name.
Maximus is the Latin root name (Wiktionary: Maximilianus derives from Maximus); a separate name in registers.
An English word-name with its own history; Wiktionary glosses Mercedes only as 'equivalent to Mercy', not as the same name.
Own Hebrew name (short for Mikhayahu); Wiktionary treats Michael only as a coordinate term, not a form.
Polish form of Nicholas, a different name (Greek Nikolaos).
A separate Slavic given name; Wiktionary gives it as borrowed from Slavic languages and never connects it to Michael.
Wiktionary gives Miles a separate Old French origin (Milo); the Michael link is only for the surname.
Wiktionary calls Portuguese Miriam a doublet of Maria; they share a Hebrew origin (Miryam) but are separate register names (Maria/Mary).
Same spelling in Latin script but a different Arabic name meaning 'dew', not the Slavic name meaning 'hope'.
